literal: Having rid of envy, those who prospered even, do not exist; that (envy) those who do not have, in prosperity, those who were ruined even, do not exist.
translation: No one has ever prospered through envy, nor has anyone free from envy ever been ruined of their prosperity.
modern: பொறாமை கொண்டு பெருமையடைந்தவர்களும் இல்லை; அந்தப் பொறாமை இல்லாதவர்களில் தம் செல்வச் செழிப்பை இழந்தவர்களும் இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute law of envy and its consequences on human fortune. The first part asserts that history has never seen anyone who truly grew great or prospered by harboring envy. Conversely, the second part states that those who are free from envy have never been ruined or deprived of their wealth. The contrast between 'அகன்றார்' (those who expanded or prospered) and 'தீர்ந்தார்' (those who were ruined or depleted) shows that envy never builds up, and the lack of envy never tears down.
